C1_two_subject.easy: In a 2014 study, linguists Asifa Majid and Niclas Burenhult asked speakers of Jahai, a language of hunter-gatherers on the Malay Peninsula, to name a series of colors and odors. The Jahai speakers named odors as readily as colors, drawing on roughly a dozen abstract smell terms. English speakers, ______ struggled to identify even familiar odors, typically offering lengthy descriptions of a possible source instead.
C2_belief_finding.easy: After the death of composer Florence Price in 1953, dozens of her scores, including works she had never managed to publish, were presumed lost, and her reputation faded. ______ in 2009, a couple renovating a dilapidated house in St. Anne, Illinois, once Price’s summer home, discovered stacks of her manuscripts, among them two violin concertos and her Fourth Symphony.
C3_limiting_fact.easy: During the 1930s and 1940s, Chinese American cinematographer James Wong Howe was one of the most sought-after camera artists in Hollywood. Studios prized his innovative techniques, particularly his expressive low-key lighting and his early experiments with deep-focus photography. ______ after being named in testimony as a Communist sympathizer, Howe was gray-listed and struggled to find employment until director Samuel Fuller hired him in 1950.
E1_consequence.easy: In 2005, cyclists in Seville, Spain, had access to only about 12 kilometers of disconnected bike paths. Over the following five years, municipal authorities constructed an interconnected network of roughly 120 kilometers of bike lanes physically separated from motorized traffic. ______ the number of daily bicycle trips in the city increased more than fivefold between 2006 and 2011.
E2_motive_action.easy: Earth and planetary scientist Britney Schmidt wanted to measure melting along the grounding line of Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier, where the ice lifts off the seafloor. Because the glacier’s floating ice shelf extends far beyond that line, ships cannot reach it. ______ in 2020 her team bored through almost 600 meters of ice and lowered a slender robot, Icefin, into the ocean below.
P1_purpose_aptness.easy: Tokyo-based architect Takaharu Tezuka wanted the children at Fuji Kindergarten, a Montessori school in suburban Tachikawa, to learn through unrestricted exploration rather than within the physical boundaries of separate classrooms. ______ he designed the school, completed in 2007, as a single continuous oval whose rooftop deck doubles as a playground and running track, with no conventional play equipment installed.
A1_addition.easy: Pura Belpré, the first Puerto Rican librarian in the New York Public Library system, championed Spanish-language storytelling. In the late 1920s, she began conducting bilingual story programs at several branches, often performing traditional folktales with handmade puppets. ______ she adapted these folktales into children’s books; her Pérez and Martina (1932) was the first Puerto Rican folktale published in the United States.
X1_example.easy: Many contemporary African artists construct monumental works from discarded consumer goods. In doing so, they invest everyday waste with new cultural and political significance. ______ Ghanaian artist Serge Attukwei Clottey cuts yellow plastic jerrycans, which were originally used to transport cooking oil and now commonly carry water, into small tiles that he binds together with copper wire to form enormous tapestries.
S1_spec_restate.easy: Enacted in 1990, the US Indian Arts and Crafts Act is a truth-in-advertising law. It restricts how art and craft products may be marketed to consumers. ______ the law makes it illegal to display or sell any such product in a manner that falsely suggests it was produced by a member of a federally or state-recognized tribe or by an artisan certified by a tribe.
M1_emphasis.easy: Kyrgyz performer Sayakbay Karalaev (1894–1971) was a manaschi, a specialist in chanting the traditional Epic of Manas, which recounts the exploits of the hero Manas, his son, and his grandson. Karalaev’s command of the epic was extraordinary. ______ the version transcribed from his performances between 1936 and 1952 contains more than 500,000 lines, roughly twenty times the length of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey combined.
T1_sequence_time.easy: At England’s Millennium Seed Bank, incoming seed collections are first kept in a drying room at 15 percent relative humidity, sometimes for as long as six months. ______ technicians clean the seeds and X-ray them, discarding any that are empty or damaged by insects. Finally, the seeds are sealed in airtight glass containers and stored in an underground vault at −20°C.
C1_two_subject.medium: Biologist Jean-Nicolas Audet and colleagues captured Barbados bullfinches at sites ranging from heavily urbanized to rural and presented them with innovative foraging problems, such as opening a drawer to obtain food. Birds from urbanized areas performed well on these tasks and also exhibited stronger immune responses. Rural bullfinches, ______ were relatively poor problem solvers and had comparatively weak immune defenses.
C2_belief_finding.medium: Most animals with a circulatory system rely on a beating heart to propel oxygen-carrying fluid through their tissues. In a 2017 study of twelve species, ______ biologist H. Arthur Woods and colleagues found that sea spiders, whose hearts are notably weak, distribute oxygen to their extremities chiefly through peristaltic contractions of gut branches extending into each of their slender legs.
E1_consequence.medium: Red blood cells strongly absorb green light, so circulating blood can betray an otherwise translucent frog resting on a leaf. In a 2022 study, biologist Carlos Taboada and colleagues found that sleeping glassfrogs remove nearly 90 percent of their red blood cells from circulation and store them in their mirror-coated liver. ______ the resting frogs become two to three times more transparent.
E2_motive_action.medium: After swollen rivers forced the precautionary evacuation of some 250,000 residents of the Dutch province of Gelderland in 1995, the country’s water authorities concluded that its rivers needed more room to discharge high water safely. ______ the Room for the River program, carried out between 2006 and 2019, relocated dikes farther inland, excavated side channels, and lowered floodplains at 34 sites.
